tasks.gr12-cold-war-origins-t1: Topic: The origins of the Cold War for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 1). Cover why it was called a Cold War, spheres of influence and Soviet satellite states, containment (the Truman Doctrine of 1947 and the Marshall Plan), the Berlin Blockade of 1948-49 and the Berlin Wall of 1961, NATO (1949) and the Warsaw Pact (1955), brinkmanship and the Cuban Missile Crisis of October 1962, and the traditional, revisionist and post-revisionist interpretations of who was to blame. Ask balanced factual and source-skills questions; never assert one interpretation as the only correct one.
tasks.gr12-cold-war-china-t1: Topic: Case study China after 1949 for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 1). Cover the People's Republic of 1 October 1949, the Sino-Soviet split, the Cultural Revolution (1966-1976) and the Red Guards, China and its neighbours (Tibet, India 1962, Vietnam, Taiwan), whether China was a superpower by Mao's death in 1976, why China restored relations with the USA (the UN seat of 1971, Nixon's visit of 1972, full relations in 1979) and Deng Xiaoping's economic reforms from 1978. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr12-cold-war-vietnam-t1: Topic: Case study Vietnam 1954-1975 for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 1). Cover the French defeat at Dien Bien Phu, the Geneva Accords and the 17th parallel, the domino theory, the Viet Cong, the three phases (1957-65, 1965-69, 1969-75), the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, the Tet Offensive of 1968, Vietnamisation, anti-war movements and Kent State, the Paris Peace Accords of 1973, the fall of Saigon in 1975, American and Vietnamese perspectives, and how the war is remembered. Ask factual, cause and source-skills questions.
tasks.gr12-cold-war-angola-t1: Topic: Africa in the Cold War: Angola for Grade 12 History (CAPS Topic 2). Cover competing spheres of influence, Portuguese colonialism and independence (11 November 1975), the MPLA, FNLA and UNITA, the civil war, the reasons and nature of involvement by the USSR, USA, Cuba, China and South Africa, regional impact, the battles of Cuito Cuanavale (1987-88) presented through the competing South African/UNITA and Angolan/Cuban accounts without declaring a winner, the New York Accords of 22 December 1988, Namibian independence (1990) and international relations after 1989. Ask about how and why accounts differ.
